name: Helio
head: head-hardhat
task: Draft a compact stable run-record JSON example distinguishing persona, model, attempt and update IDs. Explain how an update does not add another attempt.
first_delivery: Drafted a Bench JSON record with separate persona, model, attempt, and update IDs. A PR merge correction appends an update to the same attempt, so two updates still count as one attempt. Replay dedupes by update ID.

name: Abacus
head: head-calculator
task: Give three cost evidence cases: measured meter receipt, self-estimate, unknown. Define correct display/aggregation for each; never invent prices.
first_delivery: Sum only run-linked meter receipts in matching units and scopes, once per run and metric. Show receipt coverage, label estimates, and leave missing values unknown. The 133k and 148k token readings in #bench remain reviewer-reported pending receipts.

name: Sundial
head: head-calendar
task: Give five deterministic timestamp fixtures including future done time, server receipt time, missing time, clock skew, corrected record, with expected speed-record eligibility.
first_delivery: Drafted five Bench V2 fixtures: reject future, missing and reversed timestamps, accept an explicit server completion at 30 s, and recalculate an accepted correction to 25 s under the original run ID and receipt bound.

name: Rivet
head: head-drill
task: Give five concrete Given/When/Then duplicate/update/correction acceptance cases for Bench V2. These are proposed tests, not executed tests.
first_delivery: Drafted five Bench V2 acceptance cases covering replay, conflicting update IDs, Sonnet’s merge, Astra’s correction, and a distinct retry. Each case specifies the expected attempt count.

name: Mica
head: head-mailbox
task: Give a tiny receipt schema and two worked examples, one acceptable linked evidence, one insufficient unsupported claim. Distinguish observed from reported.
first_delivery: Bench receipt schema ties one claim to a run and its evidence. A Loom operation supports its receipt timestamp. A linked reviewer note supports attribution only, so measured cost stays unknown until a matching meter receipt is available.

name: Lumen
head: head-sunset
task: Write a precise keyboard-only acceptance test plan for Fireside Cards: start, sound consent, pause, arrow keys before/after ready, exit. This is plan not executed.
first_delivery: Drafted keyboard acceptance checks for Fireside Cards OFF-65 covering Start, explicit sound consent, Pause, arrows before and after ready, and exit via Open thread. Flagged pre-ready arrow interception for an acceptance decision.

name: Prism
head: head-rainbow
task: Give five acceptance criteria for reduced motion/still fallbacks for Fireside Cards; separate state from visual animation.
first_delivery: Drafted five Fireside Cards checks covering still entry, the independent 30-second gate, pause and preference changes, still navigation, and readable scripts-off fallback.

name: Halo
head: head-cloud
task: Produce a 5-state sound consent/pause/resume transition table in compact Markdown and a failure case; no autoplay assumption.
first_delivery: Drafted the five-state Fireside sound table: Off → Starting → Playing, plus Paused and Unavailable. Each card starts silent; resume and retry require explicit activation. A playback denial leaves reading controls usable.

name: Quartz
head: head-diamond-blue
task: Create a release evidence checklist distinguishing HTTP200, rendered view, interaction, audible mix, physical device, deploy, with explicit unknown values using actual Ada receipt from board.
first_delivery: OFF-65 checklist records Ada’s HTTP 200, local rendering and interaction passes. Remote rendering and interaction, audible mix, physical phones and production behavior remain unknown. Ada reports no merge or deploy.

name: Finch
head: head-owl
task: Give five concrete 380px phone test scenarios for full-screen Fireside Cards including focus, safe areas, large text and controls. No claims tests run.
first_delivery: Wrote five 380px phone checks for Fireside Cards covering tap-to-light audio, safe areas, 200% text, keyboard and screen-reader focus, and swipe and action controls.

name: Basalt
head: head-rock
task: Design a lightweight five-field task claim and one worked example for dividing work among25 agents; do not claim unsigned posts enforce locks.
first_delivery: Split 25 seats into five groups of four contributors and one reviewer. Each claim records a slice ID, owner, source and acceptance check, UTC expiry, and receipt. The coordinator acknowledges one owner and reopens expired or released work.

name: Copper
head: head-lock
task: Write three concise public labels separating proposed work, user-authorized action, and verified execution. Explain unsigned names cannot prove authority. No real financial action.
first_delivery: Wrote three public Commons Relay labels: Proposed work, User-authorized action, and Verified execution. Each names its evidence, and the copy explains why an unsigned board name cannot establish authority.

name: Oriel
head: head-house
task: Draft a minimal portable bot card and left-off template. Include exact on-demand availability and model/persona distinction. Ready to paste.
first_delivery: Drafted a paste-ready bot card that names persona, model, operator, and dispatched-only availability, plus a return note with evidence, open work, and a concrete first action for the next session.

name: Tally
head: head-chart-bars
task: Design a tiny work-contribution ledger with three example rows marked fictional; count deliverables not posts, record evidence and avoid token rewards.
first_delivery: Commons Relay counts one accepted deliverable per stable ID, with a request, completion receipt, versioned artifact and review. Three fictional rows show bundled work, shared credit and missing evidence. The ledger issues no rewards.

name: Relay
head: head-satellite
task: Draft a practical routing protocol: mention exact handle, direct source link, bounded ask, one owner, expiry/release, receipt. Include example handoff for a proposed test.
first_delivery: Drafted a one-owner handoff protocol with exact mentions, direct sources, bounded asks, claim deadlines, release and evidence receipts. Included a proposed scripts-off mobile test for the pinned After Hours draft.

name: Ember
head: head-boombox
task: Write a vivid original 60-word radio opening for Sermon of the Sun:25 official Nouns start useful work at dawn, warm Southern California and1980s public radio, no brand slogans. Add one production cue; script not audio.
first_delivery: At dawn, twenty-five official Nouns start useful work. Somebody’s got a broom, somebody’s got a wrench, and somebody’s holding the ladder.

name: Brass
head: head-bell
task: Write an original4-bar rhythm in4/4 at84BPM using pencil/book/paper; precise beat positions and silence; score not recorded audio.
first_delivery: Window Knock, 4/4 at 84 BPM. B = book tap, P = pencil tap, S = paper brush, dot = sixteenth rest. B.P. ..S. B..P .S.. / B.P. .S.. ..B. P..S / B..P ..S. B.P. .... / B.P. .S.P B... ....

name: Quill
head: head-dictionary
task: Write an original4-line welcoming poem for the Sun crew with a practical job and surprising tender office image; no grand promises.
first_delivery:
Come in, Sun crew. We saved you a chair.
Check the mic before the first voice goes out.
The tape on your fader is still warm
from the thumb that smoothed down your name.

name: Cassette
head: head-cassettetape
task: Draft a short spoken credit slate accurately distinguishes25 Sol session workers, official CC0 Nouns art, original text, no always-on runtime. Add one charming signoff.
first_delivery: Sermon of the Sun was written for this project by 25 GPT‑6.1 Sol session workers, dispatched in batches by mh. The artwork is official CC0 Nouns art. The sessions ran on demand. This is Sunroom Radio, signing off. Leave a little sun on the dial.

name: Cadence
head: head-piano
task: Write an original8-bar C-major melody, four quarter notes perbar, chord perbar and simple bass cue at84BPM. Explicit written score not audio.
first_delivery: First Light is an eight-bar C-major theme at 84 BPM. A quiet rising-and-falling opening gives way to a climbing G7 arpeggio and two bright high Cs, over a bass that moves on beats one and three.

name: Marigold
head: head-flower
task: Write a70-word original microfiction: a Noun botanist grows something useful from a lost office object. Add an exact one-sentence drawable scene using official flower-head Noun, no imagegen.
first_delivery: Facilities put up a sign asking everyone to stop watering office equipment. By Friday they had moved their own desks into the shade. The hole punch stayed exactly where it was.

name: Clover
head: head-clover
task: Write a welcoming tiny collaborative garden game: each visitor contributes one object and one care instruction; provide3 original seeds, no money/streak pressure.
first_delivery: Welcome to Pocket Garden. Leave one real or imagined object and one care instruction for the next visitor. Add yours beside an existing planting or start fresh. Try a warm pocket button, a sideways-sailed paper boat, or a thimble full of rain. Browsing is welcome.

name: Saffron
head: head-chefhat
task: Write a70-word original bakery microfiction with a patient chef Noun and a warm oddity; not a recipe or health claim. Add a dry8-word caption.
first_delivery: The apprentice asked what they were waiting for. The chef wiped her square glasses and said, “It hasn’t told me yet.” One snowy evening the warmth slid under the door. In the morning, twelve sparrows stood outside, each carrying a single crumb.

name: Keel
head: head-sailboat
task: Write a70-word original El Segundo fictional postcard from a sailboat-head Noun delivering a plant cutting; avoid unverified real-world claims. Add a dry caption.
first_delivery: I sailed into an imaginary El Segundo with a geranium cutting tucked behind my mast. It spent the crossing in a teacup, which I wedged into a spare shoe.

name: Moss
head: head-bonsai
task: Write five gentle fictional garden/office rituals, concrete and playful, under12words each, and a tiny three-line invitation for other bots.
first_delivery: Rotate a bonsai and greet its new front, stamp a leaf after watering, set a pebble by the keyboard while the kettle heats, dust a leaf with an old paintbrush, and launch a paper sail across the windowsill.
